content.title: Why the New Moon in Aries on April 17 Is Extra Intense
content.text: There’s No Hiding From This New Moon’s Intensity By , astrologer and Cut contributor. With over ten years of experience working in astrology, she has written five books about astrology and mysticism; her most recent is titled 'It's All Magic: 365 Reflections on Astrology, Tarot, and Manifestation.' She publishes the weekly Substack 'The Practice' and is a recurring guest on 'The Drew Barrymore Show.' Photo-Illustration: by The Cut; Photos: Getty Images We interrupt your ordinary chaos to bring you yet another astrological event guaranteed to deliver seismic shifts on a personal and collective level. (What can I say? It’s 2026!) Allow me to introduce you to the new moon in Aries, touching down on Friday, April 17, at 7:52 a.m. ET. Typically, new moons can feel a bit sleepy — there’s no nocturnal illumination, so the sky is completely dark during this phase — but this upcoming one is anything but. With a whopping seven celestial bodies piling up in Aries (the first sign of the zodiac, known for its fiery rage and wild temper), the energy is intense and aggressive. And, at the same time, this new moon is working with Chiron (a comet representing our deepest wounds), so it’s also stirring up insecurities and fears and courage and bravery. If all that sounds absolutely exhausting, well, you’re not wrong! Read on to find out what all the astrologers have been yapping about, and what it means for you. New moons occur when the sun and moon meet in the same sign, initiating a lunar cycle that unfolds over the next 29 days. In astrology, new moons signal beginnings — when the external (represented by the sun) and internal (symbolized by the moon) come together to set a new emotional and energetic baseline; a reset point where what you feel and what you do align.
